ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which tongue twister helps you practise /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. Five fat frogs fried five fine fish.
   B. Ten tired tigers took Tom's toys.
   C. Twin Tom twists ten twigs.
   D. Dina's dad did a dance.

2. What is a twin? (1 mark)
   A. A brother who is older
   B. A child who has no parents
   C. A person who lives next door
   D. One of two children born at the same time to the same mother

3. Which sentence uses 'the' correctly for a best one? (1 mark)
   A. She is tall the girl.
   B. She is tallest a girl.
   C. She is a the tallest girl.
   D. She is the tallest girl.

4. Which article do we use before 'honest man'? (1 mark)
   A. some
   B. an
   C. the
   D. a

5. How would you write 9 January 2016 as day, month and year? (1 mark)
   A. 9-2016
   B. 01/09/2016
   C. 2016/01/09 only
   D. 09/01/2016

6. Which sentence has correct capital letters and the correct ending? (1 mark)
   A. We went to mombasa on saturday
   B. We went to Mombasa on Saturday,
   C. We went to Mombasa on Saturday?
   D. We went to Mombasa on Saturday.

7. Which is the more polite request? (1 mark)
   A. May I borrow your pen, please?
   B. Pen now.
   C. Give me your pen.
   D. I want the pen.

8. Which word has the vowel /eɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. wait
   B. wet
   C. pen
   D. bed

9. Which word best describes Neema in the passage? (1 mark)
   A. rude
   B. lazy
   C. honest
   D. greedy

10. Which question uses the pattern correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Have we chairs enough to seat guests?
   B. Do we have enough chairs to seat the guests?
   C. Enough chairs do we to seat the guests?
   D. Do we enough have chairs to seat the guests?

11. Which is correct spelling? (1 mark)
   A. allot of
   B. a lot of
   C. alot of
   D. a lott of

12. What should you use first when learning neat print script? (1 mark)
   A. A marker
   B. A felt pen
   C. A brush
   D. A pencil

13. What does 'bleed' mean? (1 mark)
   A. To lose blood from a cut
   B. To sing
   C. To eat too much
   D. To sleep

14. Which word goes before a noun to show ownership? (1 mark)
   A. my
   B. yours
   C. hers
   D. mine

15. Which sentence would be best in the body of a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. To whom it may concern
   B. I hope you are well.
   C. Yours faithfully
   D. Sincerely, the Manager

16. Which is the correct order for the parts of a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Body, greeting, name, date
   B. Address and date, greeting, body, closing, name
   C. Name, body, date, greeting
   D. Closing, address, body, greeting

17. What does 'thin' mean? (1 mark)
   A. very old
   B. very tall
   C. With little flesh on the body
   D. very fat

18. 'She would like to be ___.' Which fits? (1 mark)
   A. a farmer
   B. farmed
   C. farming
   D. to farm

19. Which is a way of choosing a book? (1 mark)
   A. Choose the biggest only
   B. Choose the one nobody likes
   C. Read the title, cover and first page
   D. Choose a book with no words

20. In the five-finger test, four or five fingers on a page mean the book is (1 mark)
   A. empty
   B. too hard for now
   C. too easy
   D. just right

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. List the five parts of a friendly letter. (3 marks)

22. Explain what word stress is. Give one example. (2 marks)

23. List three details that a school library form may ask for. (3 marks)

24. Give two differences between a friendly letter and an SMS. (2 marks)

25. Explain what Baraka learnt from his grandmother. (4 marks)

26. Complete the sentences: (a) We have enough plates ___ (eat) the meal. (b) There is enough rice ___ (feed) the guests. (2 marks)

27. Name three polite words or phrases and say when each is used. (3 marks)

28. Give two reasons why we must fill in forms carefully. (2 marks)

29. Write two sentences beginning 'I would like to be' and give a reason in each. (3 marks)

30. Give one direct question and one indirect question about a story of a birthday party. (3 marks)

31. Give the meaning of clan, ancestor and adopt. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Five fat frogs fried five fine fish.
   Five, fat, frogs, fried and fine have /f/ and five has /v/.

2. D — One of two children born at the same time to the same mother
   Twins are two children born together to one mother.

3. D — She is the tallest girl.
   We use the before superlative words such as tallest.

4. B — an
   The h in honest is silent, so an is used.

5. D — 09/01/2016
   Day first, then month, then year.

6. D — We went to Mombasa on Saturday.
   Sentences start with a capital letter and names such as Mombasa and Saturday also need capitals.

7. A — May I borrow your pen, please?
   It uses may I and please.

8. A — wait
   Wait has /eɪ/, but wet, pen and bed have /e/.

9. C — honest
   She returned the purse and refused a reward.

10. B — Do we have enough chairs to seat the guests?
   Enough comes before the noun chairs.

11. B — a lot of
   A lot is two words.

12. D — A pencil
   A pencil allows you to rub out mistakes.

13. A — To lose blood from a cut
   A bleeding wound loses blood.

14. A — my
   My comes before a noun. Mine stands alone.

15. B — I hope you are well.
   It is a warm, friendly opening line.

16. B — Address and date, greeting, body, closing, name
   This is the standard order.

17. C — With little flesh on the body
   Thin is the opposite of plump.

18. A — a farmer
   A noun phrase follows be.

19. C — Read the title, cover and first page
   These clues show whether the book interests you.

20. B — too hard for now
   Many unknown words show that it is too hard.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Address, date, greeting, body, closing and name (address and date may be given together).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 mark for greeting and body, 1 mark for closing and name.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Word stress is the syllable we say more strongly in a word, for example the first syllable in HOS-pi-tal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the example.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name, grade, date of birth, school name, address, class teacher, head teacher (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: A letter is longer and has five parts, but an SMS is short and has a receiver, a message and a sender. A letter is better for news and feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each difference.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: He learnt that ugali and tea are not enough. A balanced diet with energy foods, body-building foods, fruit and vegetables and clean water keeps a person strong and healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct points.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) to eat (b) to feed
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Please: when asking. Thank you: when someone helps. Sorry: when we make a mistake.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each phrase with its use.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: The reader depends on the information, so a mistake may cause confusion or lost messages. Wrong information may delay help.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: I would like to be a doctor because I want to help sick people. I would like to be a runner because I love sport.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence with reason, and 1 for accuracy.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Direct: What time did the guests arrive? Indirect: Why do you think the girl was excited?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each question and 1 mark for correct types.

31. (3 marks)
   Answer: A clan is a large group of families with the same ancestor. An ancestor is a family member who lived long ago. To adopt is to take a child into your family and raise the child as your own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning.
